questions.questionText: A juice vendor sells a special fruit drink at the rate of Rs 60 per liter. This drink is prepared by mixing mango pulp and sugar syrup in the ratio of 5:3. The cost ratio of sugar syrup and mango pulp is 7:3. If the vendor makes a profit of , what is the cost price of sugar syrup per liter?

The simple interest earned on a certain sum over 2 years is Rs. 180, whereas the compound interest on the same sum, at the same annual rate for 2 years, amounts to Rs. 192. What is the annual rate of interest?
Determine the number of three-digit numbers that are divisible by neither 6 nor 7.

In a charity event, 25 participants contributed money. The average contribution per participant was Rs 30. On average, the amount contributed by the women was Rs 5 more than that contributed by the men. When the organizer, who contributed an amount between Rs 64 and Rs 106, is included, the average contribution from all male members (including the organizer) becomes equal to that of the female members. If the average contribution of the men (in rupees) is a whole number, how many women participated in the event?

A fruit vendor buys some apples at the rate of 12 apples per Rs 100 and then purchases more apples at the rate of 9 apples per Rs 100, investing an equal amount of money in both purchases. He later sells all the apples together at the rate of 10 apples per Rs 100. What is the net percentage profit or loss from this sale?

After one such cycle of price adjustments, the price of the watch is reduced by <inlineMath>{\rm{Rs}}\;42,050</inlineMath>. The same price revision is done exactly twice before the watch is finally sold for <inlineMath>{\rm{Rs}}\;9,68,832</inlineMath>. What was the initial price of the watch?

A toy shop begins its day with a certain number of toy cars, dolls, and puzzles, ensuring that there is at least one of each type. Initially, toy cars make up 40% of the total inventory. During the day, the shop manages to sell half of the toy cars, exactly 96 dolls, and 40% of the puzzles. By the end of the day, it is seen that exactly 50% of the entire toy inventory has been sold. What is the smallest possible total number of toys the shop had at the beginning of the day?

Three colleagues, Arun, Bharat, and Charan, decided to share their bottled juice with their friend David, who had none. Arun contributed 2 bottles more than Bharat, and Bharat contributed 1 bottle more than Charan. After sharing, all four of them had the same amount of juice. In appreciation, David paid a certain amount, which was then distributed among Arun, Bharat, and Charan in proportion to their contributions. As a result, Arun received three times the amount that Bharat received. The cost of each bottle of juice was Rs 25, and all transactions (both the sharing of juice and the division of money) were in whole numbers. How much money did Arun receive?

A drone is flying in a straight line, moving from point A to point B. The position vector of point A is <inlineMath>A = 4\hat i - 3\hat j + 2\hat k</inlineMath>  and the position vector of point B is  <inlineMath>B =  - 2\hat i + 5\hat j + 4\hat k</inlineMath>. A second drone starts at point C, which is located at <inlineMath>C = \hat i + \hat j - \hat k</inlineMath>  direction parallel to the line from point A to point B.

Find the direction vector of the line joining points A and B.

Find the unit vector in the direction of AB.

Direction Vector from Point A to Point B

If:

Position vector of point A is <inlineMath>\overrightarrow A  = \left\langle {{A_x},{A_y},{A_z}} \right\rangle </inlineMath> 

Position vector of point B is  <inlineMath>\overrightarrow B  = \left\langle {{B_x},{B_y},{B_z}} \right\rangle </inlineMath>

Then the direction vector from A to B is:

<inlineMath>\overrightarrow {AB}  = \overrightarrow B  - \overrightarrow A  = \left\langle {{B_x} - {A_x},{B_y} - {A_y},{B_z} - {A_z}} \right\rangle </inlineMath>

Magnitude of the Direction Vector

The magnitude (length) of vector <inlineMath>\overrightarrow {AB} </inlineMath>  is:

<inlineMath>\left| {\overrightarrow {AB} } \right| = \sqrt {{{\left( {{B_x} - {A_x}} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {{B_y} - {A_y}} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {{B_z} - {A_z}} \right)}^2}} </inlineMath>

Unit Vector in the Direction of AB

To find the unit vector (a vector with magnitude 1 pointing in the same direction), divide the direction vector by its magnitude:

<inlineMath>{\widehat u_{AB}} = \frac{{\overrightarrow {AB} }}{{\left| {\overrightarrow {AB} } \right|}} = \left\langle {\frac{{{B_x} - {A_x}}}{{\left| {\overrightarrow {AB} } \right|}},\frac{{{B_y} - {A_y}}}{{\left| {\overrightarrow {AB} } \right|}},\frac{{{B_z} - {A_z}}}{{\left| {\overrightarrow {AB} } \right|}}} \right\rangle </inlineMath>

options.text: <inlineMath> - 6\hat i + 2\hat j + 8\hat k ,\frac{{ - 6\hat i + 2\hat j + 8\hat k}}{9}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath> - 6\hat i + 8\hat j + 2\hat k,\frac{{ - 6\hat i + 8\hat j + 2\hat k}}{{10.2}}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath> - 4\hat i + 8\hat j + 6\hat k ,\frac{{ - 4\hat i + 8\hat j + 6\hat k}}{{12}}</inlineMath>
<inlineMath> - 6\hat i + 8\hat j + 2\hat k ,\frac{{ - 6\hat i + 4\hat j + 2\hat k}}{{10.5}}</inlineMath>

  • What is the equivalent resistance of the circuit?
  • Find the total current drawn from the power supply.
  • If the lights run for 4 hours each evening, what is the total energy consumed over 6 evenings?

A water distribution system controls the flow of water into a large reservoir using three inlet pipes (A, B, and C) and one outlet pipe (D). The system follows these conditions:

  1. Pipe A can fill the reservoir in 6 hours when working alone.
  2. Pipe B can fill the reservoir in 8 hours when working alone.
  3. Pipe C is twice as fast as pipe B in filling the reservoir.
  4. Pipe D drains the full reservoir in 10 hours when open.
  5. Pipe C can only be opened 30 minutes after pipe A starts running.
  6. If the reservoir reaches 75% capacity, pipe D opens automatically to prevent overflow.
  7. If pipe D remains open for more than 2 hours, it must be closed for 1 hour before reopening.

If pipes A, B, and C are opened simultaneously as per the conditions mentioned above, and pipe D starts operating only when the reservoir reaches 75% capacity, how long will it take to fill the reservoir completely?

Four of them are sitting at the four corners of a rectangular table, while the other four sit at the midpoints of the four sides. The ones at the corners face the centre, and the ones at the sides face outward. Two males are sitting at the middle of the sides and two females at the corners.

Clues:

  1. A sits diagonally opposite C.
  2. B sits in the middle of one of the sides.
  3. G sits fourth to the left of his wife, and his wife is not sitting next to A or B.
  4. H sits second to the right of her husband.
  5. H does not sit at any of the corners.
  6. Only F sits between H and D.
  7. D is the husband of A.
  8. E is male.

Who is H's husband?

A roller coaster car of mass 500 kg starts from rest at the top of a 40-meter-high hill. It descends along a frictionless track and reaches the bottom where it immediately climbs a second hill of height 25 meters. After reaching the top of the second hill, the car encounters a rough section 30 meters long, where the coefficient of kinetic friction between the wheels and the track is 0.15.

Assume gravitational acceleration <inlineMath>g = 9.8m/{s^2}</inlineMath> 

Calculate the speed of the roller coaster car at the bottom of the first hill.

Determine the speed of the car at the top of the second hill before entering the rough section.

Calculate the total work done by friction while the car travels through the rough section.

Potential energy, <inlineMath>PE = mgh</inlineMath> 

m is the mass of the roller coaster, g is the acceleration due to gravity and h is height.

Kinetic energy, <inlineMath>KE = \frac{1}{2}m{v^{^2}}</inlineMath> 

m is the mass and v is the speed of the roller coaster.

Using conservation of energy: <inlineMath>Total\;energy\;at\;the\;bottom\;of\;the\;first\;hill = Potential\;energy\;at\;the\;top\;of\;the\;second\;hill\\ + Kinetic\;energy\;at\;the\;top\;of\;the\;second\;hill</inlineMath>

This can be used to find the speed of the car at the top of the second hill before entering the rough section.
The work done by friction can be calculated using the formula:

<inlineMath>W =  - {f_k} \cdot d</inlineMath> 

<inlineMath>{f_k}</inlineMath> is the frictional force, and d is the length of rough section.

<inlineMath>{f_k} = {\mu _k} \cdot N</inlineMath> 

Where:

<inlineMath>{\mu _k}</inlineMath> is the coefficient of kinetic friction and N is the normal force

The normal force, N=mg

m is the mass of the roller coaster and g is the acceleration due to gravity.

  • At least one member must be a politician and at least one must be an economist. 
  • C and H are known to disagree on most policies and cannot appear together on the panel. 
  • B will only join the discussion if I is included. D refuses to participate if F is included. 
  • E refuses to participate if G is included. 
  • A will refuse to participate if C is included. 

Which of the following is not an acceptable panel? 

  1. A, B, F, G, H, I 
  2. C, D, F, H, G, I 
  3. B, E, F, A, H, I 
  4. A, C, D, B, H, I

A farmer wants to build and paint a cylindrical water tank to store rainwater. The tank has a diameter of 4 meters. He wants the tank to hold 50,000 liters of water. (1 cubic meter = 1,000 liters)
To reduce water evaporation, the tank will be completely covered with a conical concrete lid of the same diameter as the cylindrical tank. But its height is one tenth of the tank’s height.
Determine the amount of paint needed to cover the cylinder and its lid if 1 liter of paint covers 100 cm2 of area
The volume of a cylinder is:
<inlineMath>V = \pi {r^2}h</inlineMath>
The curved surface area of a cylinder (excluding the top and bottom) is given by:
<inlineMath>{A_{cylinder}} = 2\pi rh</inlineMath> 
r is the radius and h is the height of the cylinder
The curved surface area of the cone is given by:
<inlineMath>{A_{cone}} = \pi rl</inlineMath> where the slant height l can be calculated using the following formula:
<inlineMath>l = \sqrt {{r^2} + h_{lid}^2} </inlineMath>
r is the radius and h is the height of the cone

Which play did the one who bought ice cream get?

The economic system of any country is broadly divided into 3 main sectors: the primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, each playing a crucial function in the functioning of the economy. The number one sector entails activities that make use of natural resources, including agriculture, mining, forestry, and fishing. This sector is the inspiration of an economy, because it produces raw materials for processing. The secondary sector makes a speciality of production, reworking raw materials into completed merchandise. It is pushed via industries such as textiles, car, electronics, and chemicals, and frequently acts as the backbone of industrialisation and urbanisation.

The tertiary sector, also known as the service sector, includes industries like retail, hospitality, healthcare, schooling, information technology, and finance. Over the years, this area has seen first-rate growth, specifically in advanced economies, driven by technological improvements and changing customer demands. In emerging economies like India, the growth of the service sector has become increasingly important, as it contributes significantly to both GDP and employment.

Which of the following best summarises the passage on the sectors of the economy?

options.text: The primary sector remains the most significant in any economy due to its dominance in global markets, while the secondary and tertiary sectors have seen marginal growth due to the ongoing technological revolution.

Economic development is characterised by the shift from reliance on the primary sector to growth in the secondary and tertiary sectors, with a critical balance necessary for sustainable economic stability.

The tertiary sector’s explosive growth in emerging economies like India has been largely driven by the expansion of industrial production in the primary and secondary sectors, which has diminished the role of services in global GDP.

While the primary sector is essential for raw material extraction, the secondary and tertiary sectors have stagnated in recent years, leading to a diminishing role of industry and services in economic development.

questions.questionText:
India’s struggle for independence was not only a political movement but also a battleground of ideas. Leaders and thinkers offered various philosophies, each presenting a unique imaginative vision for India’s destiny.

On one hand, Mahatma Gandhi’s philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and civil disobedience gained massive support. He believed that ethical power and peaceful resistance could break the chains of colonial rule. His emphasis on truth, self-reliance, and rural improvement appealed to thousands throughout the country.

On the other hand, revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and Subhas Chandra Bose believed that direct action, although violent, was necessary to shake the British Empire. Bose, especially, was vocal about his disagreement with Gandhi’s strategies, arguing that freedom had to be seized, not asked for.

Both schools of thought had the same purpose and freedom, but their techniques and philosophies often stood apart. These debates not only shaped the freedom movement but also laid the ideological foundation of modern India.

 

Which of the following statements would most likely be seen as an opposing argument to Gandhi’s philosophy of non-violence?

options.text: Non-violent resistance empowers the masses and maintains moral high ground.
Civil disobedience has the potential to awaken political consciousness.
Violent revolution is a necessary tool against oppressive regimes.
Peaceful protest creates long-term social harmony.

questions.questionText:
After over thirty years, the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 represented a significant shift in India's educational system. The strategy suggested structural modifications, including the 5+3+3+4 format and the promotion of the mother tongue as the medium of instruction until Grade 5, to make education more comprehensive, adaptable, and skill-oriented. The NEP became a political hot potato for both acclaim and criticism. Advocates saw it as a long-overdue reform that brought education in line with the demands of the twenty-first century. 

Some states argued that imposing a consolidated curriculum and federal overreach diminished regional autonomy, prompting criticism. This conflict rekindled discussions about the Constitution's traditional view of education policy as a concurrent obligation between the federal government and the states. 

 

What was a major political consequence of implementing the NEP 2020?

options.text: It led to a decline in public interest in regional languages.
It caused an increase in private sector investment in schools.
It sparked debates about Centre-State power distribution in education.
It resulted in the immediate replacement of all school textbooks.

questions.questionText:
The tale of human evolution is a charming journey that spans tens of millions of years, tracing our transformation from primitive ancestors to the current Homo sapiens. The earliest recognised human-like species, Australopithecus, lived around 4 million years ago in Africa. These early hominins walked on legs; however, they had small brains and ape-like features.

Over time, species which included Homo habilis emerged, referred to as the ‘handy man’ for their capacity to create convenient stone equipment. Homo erectus had a bigger brain and mastered using fire, permitting them to emigrate out of Africa and adapt to diverse environments.
 

After reading the passage, select the correct tone of the same.

Physicians undertake varying strategies to impart medical facts to patients, formed by using cultural context, personal touches, and scientific training. In Western International locations, many medical doctors follow a patient-targeted method, emphasising transparency, shared decision-making, and empathetic communication. They regularly use visual aids, simplified language, and open-ended inquiries to make sure their patients understand.

In comparison, physicians in more hierarchical or conventional structures, which include regions of Asia or the Middle East might also depend upon authoritative verbal exchange, in which the medical doctor affords direct commands and the patient listens without tons questioning. This approach can create readability and self-assurance, in particular in time-sensitive or emergency settings, but may also limit patient engagement in long-term care.

Some doctors integrate both models, tailoring their strategies to shape the patient’s background and emotional needs. As healthcare becomes more globalised, knowledge and the ability to adapt to numerous communication styles have become essential for effective treatment and patient satisfaction.

What is the tone of the passage?

options.text: Critical – highlighting the flaws in how physicians communicate globally.
Persuasive – urging all physicians to adopt a specific communication method.
Casual – using informal language to discuss medical communication practices.
Objective – presenting a balanced comparison of different physician communication techniques.

questions.questionText:
Health isn't always simply the absence of ailment; it's a dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being. Surprisingly, many small habits have a considerable effect on our health. For example, studies have shown that giggling can enhance blood flow and reduce stress hormones while drinking enough water can dramatically improve awareness.

Sleep, frequently unnoticed, is the other pillar of fitness. Chronic sleep deprivation is linked not just to fatigue but also to weakened immunity, weight gain, and even coronary heart disease. Meanwhile, mental health has increasingly been identified to be just as important as physical fitness. Practices like mindfulness and normal social interplay have been connected to lower rates of despair and tension.

Despite these insights, there's an ongoing debate about how much control people have over their health. While life choices are essential, genetics, environmental elements, and access to healthcare all play significant roles. Recognising this balance is essential to developing a practical and compassionate approach to public health.


Which of the following pairs best represents one supporting and one opposing argument related to the idea that ‘individual lifestyle choices are the main factor in determining health’?

options.text:
Supporting: Healthy habits like laughter and hydration can improve mental and physical well-being.
Opposing: People are fully responsible for their health, regardless of circumstances

Supporting: Sleep, nutrition, and mindfulness are proven to reduce disease risk.
Opposing: Health is entirely determined by genetics and cannot be changed by behaviour.

Supporting: Everyday actions like exercise and stress reduction significantly impact overall health.
Opposing: External factors such as environment and access to healthcare also shape health outcomes.

Supporting: Lack of sleep directly causes weight gain and poor immunity.
Opposing: Good health only depends on medical intervention, not personal habits.

questions.questionText:
Psychological well-being plays a critical role in maintaining overall health and productivity. It was found in studies that individuals with good mental health are more likely to build strong relationships and cope effectively with stress. On the other hand, untreated psychological issues such as anxiety and depression can lead to severe consequences, including physical illnesses and diminished quality of life. Advocates argue that investing in mental health resources not only benefits individuals but also reduces societal costs associated with lost productivity and healthcare expenses. Critics, however, contend that limited budgets should prioritise physical health interventions, as their impact is more immediate and measurable.

Which of the following arguments supports the importance of investing in psychological well-being?

options.text: Studies suggest that individuals with good mental health are more productive and resilient.
Physical health interventions have a more immediate and measurable impact.
Mental health issues overshadow underlying physical illnesses and diminished quality of life.
Limited budgets should prioritise physical health interventions over psychological health.

questions.questionText:
Brain development has a profound impact on an individual's cognitive, emotional, and social abilities. In early childhood, rapid brain growth supports language acquisition, problem-solving, and memory skills. As children grow, the development of the prefrontal cortex enhances their capacity for reasoning, decision-making, and impulse control. Research supports the idea that positive stimuli, such as nurturing environments and educational exposure, promote healthy brain development, leading to better academic and behavioural outcomes. 

However, some researchers argue that genetic factors play a more dominant role, suggesting that while the environment influences development, it cannot override inherited traits. Others caution that overemphasising environmental factors might overlook the biological limits of development. Still, most experts agree that a combination of both nature and nurture shapes the effects of brain development throughout life.

Which of the following best identifies both a supporting and an opposing argument presented in the passage?

options.text:
Supporting: Brain development benefits from nurturing environments.
Opposing: Emotional development is not influenced by brain growth.

Supporting: Early stimulation enhances memory and problem-solving skills.
Opposing: Some experts believe schooling has little effect on brain structure.

Supporting: Educational exposure improves cognitive development.
Opposing: Overemphasis on the environment may ignore genetic limitations.

Supporting: Positive environments support brain growth and function.
Opposing: Some researchers argue that genetic factors are more influential.

questions.questionText:
Cloud storage has already revolutionised the way individuals and organisations manage data, but its future promises even more transformative shifts. One key development lies in edge-integrated cloud storage, where data processing occurs closer to the source such as IoT devices minimising latency and bandwidth use. This approach is critical for real-time applications like autonomous vehicles and smart city infrastructure.

Simultaneously, AI-powered storage management is expected to evolve rapidly. Intelligent systems could automatically organise, optimise, and secure cloud data, predicting storage needs or identifying vulnerabilities before they become critical. Moreover, decentralised cloud storage, leveraging blockchain, may offer enhanced privacy and user control by distributing data across networks rather than relying on centralised data centres. 

Which of the following inferences can most reasonably be drawn from the passage regarding the direction of cloud storage evolution?

options.text: The future of cloud storage will prioritise minimising hardware dependence by eliminating edge devices and decentralising all processes.
Advancements in cloud storage are primarily aimed at increasing storage space rather than enhancing security, speed, or accessibility.
The integration of edge computing, AI, and decentralised systems reflects a broader trend toward making cloud storage more intelligent, efficient, and secure.
As cloud storage becomes more complex, it will require users to manually manage and secure their data without algorithmic assistance.

questions.questionText:
Throughout history, humans have used distinctive forms of government to organise their societies. In historical times, monarchies had been the most commonplace. Kings and queens dominated their lands, frequently claiming that their power came from the gods. They established control via armies and handed their rule down to their children.

Over time, people started exploring new approaches to governing. In ancient Greece, the concept of democracy was introduced, permitting residents to have a say in decision-making. The Roman Republic followed a comparable system, where leaders were elected to represent the citizens. However, these structures were volatile, and many became empires with rulers protecting absolute power.

In the twentieth century, distinct political systems emerged. Some countries embraced democracy, while others experimented with communism, socialism, or authoritarian rule. Today, governments worldwide maintain the balance of power between leaders and citizens in extraordinary ways.

Which of the following best explains how new political ideas in the 17th and 18th centuries influenced government systems?

options.text: They strengthened the authority of kings by emphasising the importance of absolute power.
They shifted focus away from governance and toward economic growth as the key to national success.
They led to uprisings that replaced monarchies with governments based on popular representation.
They encouraged rulers to expand their military to prevent political reforms.

questions.questionText:
The Global Financial Crisis of 2007–2008, triggered by the collapse of the U.S. housing market and the subprime mortgage crisis, had far-reaching effects across economies worldwide. While India was not at the epicentre of the crisis, its financial and economic systems felt its repercussions due to increasing globalization and interdependence. 

The Crisis led to a decline in foreign investment, reduced export demand, and stock market volatility, affecting major industries such as IT, real estate, and manufacturing. The Indian economy, however, showed resilience due to strong domestic consumption, a well-regulated banking sector, and timely government interventions such as stimulus packages and interest rate adjustments. 

Despite a temporary slowdown in GDP growth and employment rates, India managed to recover faster than many Western economies, highlighting the strength of its internal market and financial safeguards.

Based on the passage, which of the following can be inferred about India's economic response to the 2007 Crisis?

options.text: India's economic downturn was as severe as that of the United States, requiring large-scale government bailouts to prevent financial collapse.
The Crisis led to a permanent decline in India’s foreign investments and exports, forcing the country to shift to a completely self-reliant economic model.
While India was impacted by the Crisis, its recovery was aided by a combination of internal economic strengths and government interventions.
India's financial system was completely unaffected by the 2007 Global Crisis due to its isolated and independent economic structure.

The tale of human evolution is a charming journey that spans tens of millions of years, tracing our transformation from primitive ancestors to the current Homo sapiens. The earliest recognised human-like species, Australopithecus, lived around 4 million years ago in Africa. These early hominins walked on legs; however, they had small brains and ape-like features.

Over time, species which included Homo habilis emerged, referred to as the ‘handy man’ for their capacity to create convenient stone equipment. Homo erectus had a bigger brain and mastered using fire, permitting them to emigrate out of Africa and adapt to diverse environments.

Indian politics has experienced significant transformation over the decades. In the early years post-independence, the political landscape was primarily dominated by the Indian National Congress, which played a central role in shaping the country's democratic foundations. However, over time, there has been a shift towards a multi-party system, with regional and smaller political parties gaining influence. This change has been particularly evident in the last few decades, as regional parties have increasingly secured power in various states, challenging the dominance of national parties. 

One of the key factors behind this shift has been the rise of identity-based politics, where issues like caste, religion, and language have been used to mobilise voters. As a result, coalition governments have become more common, leading to a more fragmented political environment. This has led to both positive and negative consequences, such as increased representation of diverse groups but also political instability and difficulty in policy implementation.

Based on the passage, which of the following best represents the cause-and-effect relationships discussed?

options.text: The dominance of national parties has led to increased political fragmentation and instability.
Political instability in India has resulted in the increased influence of smaller political parties.
The shift towards a multi-party system has resulted in a more centralised political environment.
The rise of identity-based politics has led to the formation of more coalition governments, which have caused political instability.

questions.questionText:
The Yamuna River, which flows through Delhi, faces severe pollution due to industrial waste, sewage discharge, and encroachments. Despite government initiatives like the Yamuna Action Plan, high levels of toxic chemicals and untreated sewage continue to degrade water quality. The river's dissolved oxygen levels remain critically low, affecting aquatic life and making the water unfit for consumption. Experts emphasise the need for stricter regulations, better waste management, and community participation to restore the Yamuna to a healthier state.

Which of the following is the primary cause of Yamuna River’s pollution in Delhi?

options.text: Seasonal changes affecting the river's natural filtration ability.
Lack of awareness among local communities about water conservation.
Increasing urbanisation, leading to higher waste disposal in the river.
Agricultural runoff carries excessive nutrients into the river.

questions.questionText:
Passage:

Education is now not a one-size-fits-all. Personalised studying, an approach tailored to male or female college students' strengths, wishes, and pastimes, is reshaping classrooms around the world. With the assistance of technology, teachers can now track each student’s progress in real time, imparting focused lessons and resources to close gaps or address challenges wherein needed. Adaptive knowledge platforms regulate content material based on a pupil’s performance, ensuring they learn at their own pace.

This method empowers college students to take ownership of their studying journey, fostering independence and motivation. For example, a scholar struggling with maths would possibly receive interactive tutorials. Personalised teaching also supports various learning styles; visual learners can discover movies, auditory learners can interact with podcasts, and hands-on inexperienced persons can address practical responsibilities.

Which of the following best summarises the passage on personalised learning?

options.text: Personalised learning relies entirely on technology to replace traditional teaching, making education faster and more efficient for all students.
Personalised learning tailors education to each student’s strengths and needs, using technology and flexible strategies to promote independent, diverse, and effective learning experiences.
Personalised learning focuses on helping struggling students catch up, though it may neglect those who are already performing well.
Personalised learning is a temporary trend that creates more challenges for teachers than benefits for students.

questions.questionText:
A capitalist form of government often touts its fidelity to individual liberty, free markets, and limited state intervention. In theory, it champions merit, enterprise, and innovation, allowing economic actors the freedom to shape their destinies. Yet, this ideological celebration obscures an enduring paradox. While capitalism demands minimal governance in theory, in practice, it relies heavily on institutional scaffolding: legal systems to enforce contracts, central banks to stabilise markets, and regulatory bodies to manage crises born from its very excesses.

Capitalism often reconfigures governance itself not through overt authoritarianism, but via the subtle consolidation of influence. Policy decisions, while appearing democratic, may be increasingly skewed by concentrated wealth and corporate lobbying, blurring the lines between economic freedom and oligarchic control. Public services may shrink under the guise of efficiency, while market outcomes often unequal and volatile become treated as moral verdicts rather than systemic consequences.

What is the predominant tone of the passage?

options.text: Idealistic and persuasive – highlighting the virtues of capitalism through reasoned argument.
Critical and reflective – acknowledging capitalist strengths while unpacking systemic contradictions.
Neutral and descriptive – outlining features of capitalism without evaluative language
Cynical and dismissive – portraying capitalism as fundamentally deceptive and unworkable.

questions.questionText:
Ethics is frequently seen as a machine of right and wrong, however, psychology indicates that our moral selections are hardly ever merely logical. Instead, they are shaped by emotions, upbringing, social surroundings, and even unconscious biases. People don’t usually comply with moral regulations due to the fact that they understand them; they frequently follow them because they experience remorse while breaking them, or because society rewards certain behaviours. 

Psychologists argue that ethics isn't always only a philosophical idea, but a set of behaviours shaped by cultural values and mental patterns. What’s visible as moral in one society can be judged in a different way in every other. This doesn’t suggest that ethics are meaningless; however, it suggests that information about how human beings behave is essential to constructing a genuinely moral society.
 

Which of the following best summarises the central idea of the passage?

options.text: Ethical behaviour is mostly taught through childhood rules and rarely changes later in life.
Ethical decisions are influenced by personal emotions, social settings, and cultural values, not just logic or universal rules.
Ethics is a fixed set of principles agreed upon by all societies and enforced by psychological pressure.
People follow ethics only because they fear punishment or judgment by others in society.

questions.questionText:
The Ganga River, also known as the Ganges, is one of the most sacred and significant rivers in India. Originating from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas, it flows through northern India and Bangladesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. The river supports the livelihoods of millions of people by providing water for agriculture, industry, and domestic use. However, over the years, excessive pollution from industrial waste, sewage, and religious offerings has severely affected its water quality. As a result, efforts like the ‘Namami Gange’ mission have been launched to clean and conserve the river.

What is the most accurate cause-and-effect relationship described in the passage?

options.text: The Ganga flows through northern India because it is sacred.
The Ganga supports agriculture because it is a long river.
Pollution has increased due to growing population and industrial activities
The Namami Gange mission was launched to promote tourism.

questions.questionText:
The anti-globalisation movement emerged prominently in the late 20th century as a response to the growing influence of global economic institutions and multinational corporations. Critics within the movement argue that globalisation, while promoting free trade and economic integration, often comes at the expense of local economies, workers' rights, environmental sustainability, and cultural diversity. They point to policies promoted by institutions like the International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Trade Organisation (WTO), and World Bank, which they believe prioritise corporate profits and economic growth over social justice and ecological balance.

Protesters and activists have raised concerns about how trade liberalisation can lead to job losses, wage suppression, and the erosion of national sovereignty. They argue that developing nations are particularly vulnerable to exploitation, with local industries unable to compete with foreign imports and labour subjected to poor conditions in export-oriented economies. Moreover, the environmental cost of mass production and transportation is seen as a direct consequence of unregulated global trade.

Which of the following best reflects a cause-and-effect relationship described in the passage?

options.text: The establishment of the World Bank and IMF was caused by the anti-globalisation protests of the early 2000s.
Concerns over job losses, environmental harm, and cultural erosion have led activists to oppose the unregulated spread of global trade.
The anti-globalisation movement succeeded in halting all international cooperation and trade agreements.
Multinational corporations expanded globally because of labour unions and environmental regulations.

questions.questionText:
Psychologists have long studied what makes some individuals consistently happy. One key reason lies in the power of positive thinking; people who focus on the good in every situation tend to experience greater emotional well-being. Gratitude is another powerful factor; those who regularly express appreciation for life’s small and large blessings often report higher levels of happiness. Additionally, having a strong sense of purpose and engaging in meaningful activities contribute significantly to lasting joy. Social connection also plays a vital role; interacting with friends and family boosts mood and provides emotional support. Lastly, practising mindfulness helps individuals stay grounded in the present, reducing stress and promoting inner peace. Together, these habits form the foundation for a joyful mindset.

After reading the passage, select the correct tone of the same.
